thesis: Honeywell Aerospace has successfully spun off as a standalone tier‑1 supplier and reports a growing order backlog and maintained organic sales guidance. However, the company now carries a substantial new senior‑note debt load, faces continued supply‑chain constraints, and incurs ongoing trademark‑license payments. The lack of disclosed quantitative growth rates and margins prevents a clear assessment of profitability and valuation, leaving the investment case uncertain.
risks: Supply‑chain constraints could impair delivery and increase costs.
High leverage from the recent senior‑note issuance may limit financial flexibility.
Trademark‑license payments to Honeywell add a recurring expense.
Macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical tensions could affect demand.
Litigation and other contingent liabilities could materialize unexpectedly.
insight: Backlog at quarter end was $19.3 billion, up 12 % from the prior year, providing a sizable order pipeline — EX-99.1 line 38: “Backlog | | $19,324 | | $17,255 | | 12%”
